profile.facility_type_note: The Westin Building at 2001 Sixth Avenue, downtown Seattle (Digital Realty's SEA10), is one of the most important internet exchange and carrier hotel buildings on the US West Coast, historically known as the Westin Building Exchange. Digital Realty acquired a controlling stake in the building, per Data Center Frontier and Commercial Property Executive coverage of the transaction. The Intergate facility in Tukwila is a separate building from the downtown Westin Building; Digital Realty also operates a facility (SEA1) at 3433 S 120th Place in the Seattle/Tukwila area per datacenterHawk.

reading.body:
The Westin Building (SEA10) is a 412,500 square foot carrier hotel and internet exchange point in downtown Seattle, operated by Digital Realty. No critical IT load in megawatts is published for this facility. The building holds N+1 cooling redundancy, a specification that qualifies it to host tenants requiring fault tolerance but does not indicate current utilization or planned expansion.

Washington state has 46 mapped data center facilities, of which only 2 publish power specifications totaling 60 MW. This campus ranks third among facilities with published capacity in the state, meaning it either publishes a figure lower than two others or no figure at all. Without published megawatts, its position in the state ranking reflects incomplete disclosure rather than measured technical scale.

As a colocation carrier hotel in a major tech hub, SEA10 likely matters to regional connectivity and serves as an internet exchange rather than as a dedicated AI training campus. The absence of published power capacity suggests the facility operates in a market segment where tenants, not operators, drive specifications. To assess its relevance to AI scaling, a reader would need to know the critical IT load the building can sustain, information not disclosed on Digital Realty's spec page.
